$comment: T-FT-WEB-CHUNK-SEQ-RACE cross-surface vectors (RESUME-PROTOCOL v3.0 RULE 30).
One file, two consumers:
- tests/e2e-ft-chunk-seq-contract.test.mjs (web: the REAL createFailClosedSender from
lib/e2e/session.mjs, driven with N seals IN FLIGHT TOGETHER the way lib/fileTransfer
/sender.ts pump() drives it)
- dnkdialer-android/app/src/test/java/com/dnkdialer/companion/E2eFtChunkSeqContractTest.kt
(phone: the REAL E2eDedupe.observe over the SAME `s` sequences)
THE ROW THIS FILE EXISTS FOR IS three-chunks-in-flight. On PROD 8e0c035 the browser sealed
three FILE_CHUNKs within 7 ms; createFailClosedSender read its counter, awaited the durability
commit, and only then advanced it, so all three were handed the SAME `s`. The phone stored
chunk 0, dropped chunk 1 as `duplicate` (E2eDedupe) and then refused chunk 2 as out-of-order,
and the transfer died with no FILE_COMPLETE (live-acceptance-8e0c035-20260923T1856Z).
`emitted` is what the browser puts on the wire; `verdicts` is what E2eDedupe answers, one per
emitted `s`, in order. The BUG rows are kept deliberately: they are the only thing that proves
the phone half was behaving correctly all along and that a regression of the web half would be
caught HERE rather than on a live acceptance run.
A duplicated `s` is not merely a dropped chunk. Under mode ON the nonce is derived from the
session prefix and the sequence number, so two frames under one `s` is GCM nonce reuse.

rows.label: THE DEFECT: three chunks sealed back-to-back must carry three DIFFERENT, strictly increasing s
What the browser actually emitted before the fix: one s for all three. The phone was right to drop two.
SENDER_ACK_WINDOW + 1 chunks in flight — the real ceiling of pump()'s burst
A resumed counter keeps its floor: a burst after a reattach must not restart at 0
The degenerate case the old code did get right, pinned so the fix cannot break it
The relay's frameBuffer replays on resume: a repeated s is a DROP, never a refusal
M-A5-2 is untouched by this lane: a jump past the window is REFUSED, not deduped

$comment: Persist-before-emit (A1 rule 3) survives the fix. Reserving the sequence synchronously is
only half of it: the durability commits must also LAND in the order the sequences were
reserved, or a crash would leave a stored floor that is not the highest number handed out —
the same counter-reuse hazard, one reload later. The web suite asserts the commit stream.
